- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.16 or 79.68), then corrects with a downward bias.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion toward recent lower levels.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth; fails to capture volatility or sudden reversals in the true outcome.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — often underreacts or delays correction.
- High bias in the middle of the forecast (days 10–20) — overestimates when true values are trending down.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the last 5–7 days, possibly due to momentum or model drift.
- Model fails to adjust for recent high volatility — overconfident in smooth trend continuation.
